sections.heading: Making Dua for Righteous Offspring
sections.content: Throughout pregnancy, make sincere dua asking Allah for a healthy, righteous child. The Prophet (PBUH) taught us that children are a trust from Allah.
sections.reference: وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ

sections.heading: Reciting Quran
sections.content: Recite Quran regularly, especially Surah Maryam and Surah Yusuf. The baby can hear sounds in the womb, and Quran recitation brings barakah.

sections.heading: Good Character and Halal Food
sections.content: Maintain good character, eat halal and tayyib food, and avoid haram. What the mother consumes and how she behaves affects the child.

sections.heading: Adhan and Iqamah
sections.content: Recite the Adhan in the baby's right ear and Iqamah in the left ear. This is a beautiful Sunnah that welcomes the baby with the words of Allah's greatness.
sections.reference: The Prophet (PBUH) called Adhan in the ear of Al-Hasan when Fatimah gave birth to him.

sections.heading: Tahnik (Sweet Date)
sections.content: Soften a date and rub a small amount on the baby's palate with your finger. This follows the Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH).

sections.heading: Choosing a Good Name
sections.content: Choose a beautiful Islamic name with good meaning within 7 days. The child will be called by this name on the Day of Judgment.

sections.heading: Aqiqah (Sacrifice)
sections.content: Perform Aqiqah on the 7th day. Sacrifice 2 sheep for a boy and 1 for a girl. Distribute the meat to the poor and share with family.
sections.details: This is an act of gratitude to Allah and provides food for the needy.

sections.heading: Shaving the Hair
sections.content: Shave the baby's hair on the 7th day and give charity equal to the weight of the hair in silver.
sections.reference: This is a Sunnah that brings barakah and cleanses the child.

sections.heading: Circumcision (Khitan)
sections.content: For boys, circumcision is an important Sunnah. It is recommended to do it on the 7th day, but can be done later.

duas.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
duas.translation: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from every devil, harmful thing, and every evil eye.
duas.reference: Said by Prophet Ibrahim (AS) for his sons

duas.translation: O Allah, in Your Name I die and I live.

duas.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
duas.translation: All praise is for Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us, and unto Him is the resurrection.

duas.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
duas.translation: All praise is for Allah who fed me this and provided it for me without any might or power from myself.

principles.title: Teach Tawhid First
principles.description: The first thing to teach your child is the belief in One Allah. Let 'La ilaha illallah' be among their first words.
tips: Make it part of daily routine
Explain in simple terms as they grow

principles.title: Love and Mercy
principles.description: Show love, kindness, and mercy. The Prophet (PBUH) was very gentle with children. Kiss them, hug them, and spend quality time.
principles.reference: The Prophet (PBUH) kissed children and said 'He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy'

principles.title: Teach Salah Early
principles.description: Command children to pray at age 7, and encourage practice before that through example and gentle teaching.
principles.reference: Hadith: 'Teach your children to pray when they are seven years old'

principles.title: Good Character (Akhlaq)
principles.description: Teach honesty, kindness, respect, and good manners. Character is the foundation of faith.
tips: Tell stories of Prophets and Sahaba

principles.title: Quran Connection
principles.description: Build love for Quran from a young age. Recite to them, teach them short surahs, and enroll them in Quran classes.

principles.title: Balance and Moderation
principles.description: Islam is balanced. Allow play, fun, and childhood while teaching deen. Don't be too harsh or too lenient.
principles.reference: The Prophet (PBUH) played with children and raced with his wife

islamicStoriesForKids.description: Islamic stories and prophets stories for children
